- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was neutral or positive prior — cap forecast at 1-2% below peak or use moving average smoothing.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment mixed or neutral), model often fails to correct downward trend — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 3-day window if price is above 10-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts — use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment) to dampen volatility.
- If sentiment is high but price is falling, model often ignores sentiment — force a slight upward correction to align with sentiment momentum.
- If sentiment is low but price is rising, model often ignores sentiment — force a slight downward correction to reflect sentiment drag.
